input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The new Windows accounting export tool almost certainly produces CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings (or a BOM), and `parseStatement` in `src/ingest/parser.ts` only splits on `"\n"`, leaving a stray `\r` attached to the last field of the header/row. That mismatches the expected column shape and triggers `errors.rowShape` ("Malformed row...") on the very first row every time, even though the file looks fine in a spreadsheet. The parser needs to normalize line endings (and strip a leading BOM) before splitting into rows/columns.

text: This confirms the parser file is the main suspect. The file src/ingest/parser.ts handles CSV parsing and splits only on "\n", not accounting for Windows-style CRLF line endings or possible delimiter differences from the new export tool—this is the likely root cause of the bug.
